summary.headline: LT Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore, with EBITDA up 20% to INR363 crore but margin down to 11.5% from 12.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore (19% normalised), with gross profit up 19% to INR1,029 crore and PAT up 9% to INR183 crore. Core basmati and specialty rice revenue rose 34% to INR2,845 crore on 11% volume growth at a stable 13% EBITDA margin. Organic foods revenue fell to INR254 crore at a 4% EBITDA margin during restructuring to a direct-to-retailer CPG model. Management said results are in line with annual estimates and reiterated full-year guidance, with the organic recovery expected over 1.5 years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 12.1% in the prior-year period (stated as 11%)

segments.name: Core basmati and specialty rice
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,845 crore, up 34% YoY on 11% volume growth, with EBITDA margin stable at 13%. India revenue grew 23% YoY; market share 23.1% and household penetration 64.4 lakh households.

segments.name: International (incl. North America)
segments.commentary: Contributed 71% of consolidated revenue. North America grew 49% (29% normalised); Middle East and rest of world grew 44%. Europe/UK are in an investment phase with margin pressure from logistics costs.

segments.name: Organic foods and ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue INR254 crore after a temporary decline during the shift from wholesale to direct retailer (CPG) sales. EBITDA margin 4%; management guides to 7-8% by year-end and double digits later.

segments.name: Ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook (RTH/RTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 13% YoY, with biryani kits up 42%. The US RTH facility is expected to become operational this quarter; breakeven is targeted at INR400 crore revenue within 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 results are in line with annual estimates and the company is on track across all financial parameters for the full year.
Organic EBITDA is expected to reach INR70-80 crore by year-end, with margin rising to 7-8% and returning to double digits; full recovery in growth and margin targeted for FY27-FY28.
Medium-term segment growth guidance: basmati 10-12%, RTH 15-20% (small base), organic 10-12%.
FY30 ambition is more than doubling India revenue with expanding margins; RTH revenue to double in about 3 years.
Basmati EBITDA margin historically 13-14%, with a plus or minus 1% variance possible if crop inflation occurs.
Middle East growth expected around 15% from a small base.
capex_capacity: Capacity doubled for ready-to-heat products; US RTH facility expected to become operational in Q1 FY27.
Organic capacity expanded in Europe, with a plant set up and a full sales organisation built there.
No capex planned yet for the newly opened Australia entity, which has received a very small equity infusion.
Rice inventory 346,000 tonnes at an average of INR56/kg and paddy inventory 164,000 tonnes at INR38/kg as of 26 June, described as sufficient for the next year's branded demand.
Quarterly volumes: India 109,000 tonnes; international 117,000 tonnes.
demand_pricing: US tariff on rice fell from about 50% to 10%, which management says reduced the margin distortion from tariffs; pricing volatility from tariffs is now normalising.
Rice revenue growth (32-34%) was above volume growth (11%), driven by commodity inflation pass-through and US duty.
Management said it is charging a premium in basmati and Sona Masoori in organic versus competitors.
Freight rates to the Middle East rose from $200 to $4,000 per container; the competitive landscape limited pass-through there.
Logistics cost was 4.7% of revenue in Q1 FY27 after one-offs (damage retention) in Q4 FY26 phased out.
Nielsen methodology change cited for the India market share decline from 23.7% in FY26 to 23.1%; management claims share gains in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino on the crop, and whether margins are at risk from inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80-85% of basmati area relies on canal or groundwater irrigation and 14-15% on rain. About 20% of area faces issues; a clearer crop picture is expected by mid-to-end August. Costs would be passed on to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary gross and EBITDA margins fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to the shift from CIF to C&I shipment terms with a related US subsidiary and a drop in organic gross margin from 35% to 33%. Management said consolidated gross margin improved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR419 crore to INR486 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the increase reflects Golden Star, now 100% owned, being consolidated from this quarter. Previously it was not consolidated, so both revenue and expenses rose.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US growth net of discounts, with discounts still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales are recorded net of promotions and discounts under accounting rules, so the reported growth is already net.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior quarter included a one-off gain from revaluation of investments, which has not recurred; other income is now normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did organic margin fall and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model moved from wholesalers to direct retail, with a new Europe plant and sales organisation. Margin is 4% now, targeted at 7-8% by year-end, and expected back in double digits in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much more working capital can be released from supplier financing?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is near optimum supplier financing, with perhaps 4-5 days of further room but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India's market share falling and will the top two players lose share to the third?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to a Nielsen methodology change. It claims share gains this quarter, with about 40%+ share on e-commerce platforms and a 20 lakh household increase last year.

risks_watch: El Nino and irrigation: crop size clarity expected by mid-to-end August; management says about 20% of basmati area faces issues and a lower crop would bring inflation, which it expects to pass on to consumers.

Organic recovery execution: margin is 4% now, targeted at INR70-80 crore EBITDA and 7-8% margin by year-end, with a return to double digits over about 1.5 years (FY27-FY28); organic gross margin fell from 35% to 33%.
US RTH facility start-up this quarter; RTH breakeven at INR400 crore revenue targeted in 2-3 years, and management acknowledged the US RTH ramp has weighed on segment margin.
Logistics and geopolitical costs: Middle East freight rose from $200 to $4,000 per container, and Europe/UK margins are under pressure; pass-through is uncertain in the Middle East.
Market share: India share fell from 23.7% in FY26 to 23.1%, which management attributes to a Nielsen methodology change; it claims share gains this quarter, which is not yet independently verified.
Working capital headroom: management sees only about 4-5 days of further supplier-financing room; US tariff refund eligibility is partly received but not yet booked.
key_quotes: So the previous rate, 10%, has continued for after that expiry as well.
So in terms of changing our route to market earlier, we were selling to the wholesaler. Now we are directly selling to the retailer, which we call CPG.
So it is the breakeven that will be coming at a revenue size of INR400 crores.
So there is no impact of demand and on the margin side also.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core basmati and India/US franchise, with specific numbers on growth and share. Cautious and less specific on organic margins, Europe/UK profitability, Middle East inroads and the El Nino crop outlook, where answers were qualified with "too early to project" and "by mid-August".
